When adding a new entry, please add it in alphabetical/lexical order
so that it's easier for future developers to find. Please also add alias
strings in alphabetical/lexical order. Set the name to nil if it would
otherwise be identical to page. If there are no aliases (aside from name
and page), set aliases to nil. Do NOT add ambiguous strings to alias
string tables. For the purposes of this comment, "ambiguous" means that
a fan might think it refers to a different character/entity. The meaning
doesn't have to be immediately obvious, so long as it does not lead to
an incorrect assumption. For example, "Ba" is ambiguous because it could
refer to Ba'alzamon, Balthamel, Bain, Bair, Balwer, etc. "Eg" is
unambiguous because everyone knows it refers to Egwene (even though
characters like Egeanin exist).
Do not add the values of name or page to the aliases string table.
Be VERY CAREFUL about correcting typos in aliases fields - alias string
tables deliberately include typos to robustly handle poorly-written wiki
code.
Do NOT remove accurate entries from alias string tables unless they are
duplicated by name or page - doing so may break e.g. quotes for that
character/entity.
README: When adding a new quote entry, first check if the quote is already here.
If so, and if the description/topic are acceptable, simply add tags,
refs, or what-have-you to it. If the speakers, addressees, description,
and/or topic are missing, just add them. If there's already a description
and/or topic, consider carefully whether to (a) modify the existing
description/topic, or (b), create a new copy of the quote with your
preferred description/topic. There's not much point in creating a copy of
a quote unless the new quote has a different set of tags or different
description (or fields used to produce the description). Try to keep
tags lexically sorted for readability.
If the quote is already here, but it contains more or less context and
you think it's worth having a separate quote for your super/sub-quote,
add a new quote entry.

When there's a 
 tag or newline in a string, put the rest of the
string on the next line and concatenate the two with the .. Lua operator.
This vastly improves the readability of this file. For an example, search
for "Ravens and crows" in this file.
Quote text:
Quote text can be provided in two forms.
Plain quote
A plain quote is a simple string. This is by far the most common use
case.
Quote Interchange
A quote interchange represents an "interchange" between two or more
characters. The most common form would be a conversation, but
interchanges don't have to be dialogue. For an example of a pure
conversation, search for "I am describing her" in this file. For an
example of an interchange that is not a pure conversation, search for
"that dress you are wearing is green" in this file.
Because lines in interchanges are not necessarily dialogue, the
automatic addition of quotes can be skipped by setting the
'quote_marks' field to false. For an example, search for
"Egwene frowned at the nonsense" in this file.
Interchanges are written as an table of (typically) single-entry
tables. Each of the single entry tables is a map from a participant
(typically a character) to some quoted text.
Participants in interchanges are automatically added to the quote
description if no description is provided.
Participants in interchanges are automatically added to the tags.
Tagging:
Tags are used for filtering/searching quotes.
Guiding principle: Only tag a quote if it would make sense for it to
appear on a page dedicated to the tag.
This means a person/concept/item shouldn't be tagged on every single
quote that relates to them. That is, a statement made to Alice
shouldn't be tagged with "Alice" unless the fact that it was said to
her actually has some significance. For example, it makes sense to tag
Kiruna on "Kneel..." because she is Aes Sedai and it is significant
that someone would tell an Aes Sedai to kneel. But it doesn't make
sense to tag Lews Therin on every quote related to the Dragon Reborn.
Conceptual tags don't have to actually describe the content of the
quote. In particular, "romance" should be used on any quote relating to
romantic relationships in general or any relationship-related
interaction between a particular involved pair that is in some way
romantically involved, including such things as exasperated or angry
exclamations.
Similarly, "humorous" can be added even if the content of the quote
itself isn't humorous, but the context (or description) of the quote
makes it so. For example, quoting Thom's statement that gleemen aren't
dangerous isn't humorous, but it becomes so if the description/topic
notes that this was said right before he killed Galldrian.
A quote should be tagged with "proverb" if it is phrased properly as a
proverb, regardless of whether it is an established in-universe proverb
or merely a clever statement made up on the spot by a character.
However, such tagged quotes should be free of particulars. For example,
virtually no quote that names a character should be tagged as a
proverb.
Do not add equivalent variations of a tag. For example, do not tag Rand
and Rand al'Thor. The aliases above will handle it as long as one of
Rand's aliases is included.
Generally, avoid tagging proper nouns that are mentioned in the quote,
description, or topic. These can be gleaned programmatically and don't
need to be added manually.
"Dragon" and "Dragon Reborn" are separate tags.
"Dragon" should be tagged on quotes that relate to the Dragon as a
concept, or to quotes by or related to Rand/Lews in their roles as the
Dragon.
"Dragon Reborn" should be tagged on quotes that relate to the Dragon
Reborn as a concept, or to Rand in his role as the Dragon Reborn.
Ask "Would it make sense for this quote to link to the Dragon and/or
Dragon Reborn pages?"
Tag a quote as "thought" if the original text contains italicized
internal thoughts. Tag a quote as "quasi-thought" if it's clearly
conveying a character's thoughts in prose.
Tag a quote as "quotation" if it's a character quoting a proverb or
someone else, or if it's e.g. a quote fragment from an in-universe
document.
Tag a quote with "!QOTD" if it shouldn't be used as a quote of the
day (e.g. it's too long to fit well in the QOTD box).
Do NOT remove tags unless you're confident it's the correct decision.
Removing the last instance of a tag may cause error boxes to appear
on pages that try to use that tag for searching/filtering.
Speakers, addressees, and pseudosources are automatically added to the
tags. If a speaker or addressee or pseudosource should not be tagged,
add the "!X" tag, where X is the name of the speaker, addressee, or
pseudosource.
Do NOT add quotes from memory. You are not a computer, and even the best
of us will fall victim to misattribution, misleadingly incorrect
phrasing, and Mandela effects. For example, Mat Cauthon never actually
speaks the words "It's time to toss the dice" and Lan never actually says
"Death is lighter than a feather, duty heavier than a mountain." (Though
he thinks it once and Nynaeve does say that she heard that exact saying
from him [off-screen]).
If you are unable or unwilling to directly copy or transcribe from the
original source, please do NOT add the quote to this file. Instead,
please leave it as a suggestion in a comment or on a Talk page.
Add book sources under book_refs even if the description/topic notes the,
book/chapter. This will be used for searching/filtering at some point.

quotes.quote: The [[Shadow]] shall rise across the world, and darken every land, even to the smallest corner, and there shall be neither [[Light]] nor safety. And [[Rand|he]] who shall be born of the [[Car'a'carn|Dawn]], born of the [[Far Dareis Mai|Maiden]], according to [[Karaethon Cycle|Prophecy]], he shall stretch forth his hands to catch the Shadow, and the world shall scream in the pain of salvation. All Glory be to the [[Creator]], and to the Light, and to he who shall be born again. May the Light save us from him.

quotes.description: from ''[[Commentaries on the Prophecies of the Dragon]]'', by [[Jurith Dorine]], Right Hand to the Queen of [[Almoren]], {{ab|742}}, the [[Third Age]]
quotes.quote: And [[Rand|his]] paths shall be many, and who shall know his name, for he shall be born among us many times, in many guises, as he has been and ever will be, time without end. His coming shall be like the sharp edge of the plow, turning our lives in furrows from out of the places where we lie in our silence. The breaker of bonds; the forger of chains. The maker of futures; the unshaper of destiny.
quotes.pseudosource: Commentaries on the Prophecies of the Dragon

quotes.quote: With [[Dragon Reborn|his]] coming are the dread fires born again. The hills burn, and the lands turn sere. The tides of men run out, and the hours dwindle. The wall is pierced, and the veil of parting raised. Storms rumble beyond the horizon, and the [[The Fires of Heaven|fires of heaven]] purge the earth. There is no salvation without destruction, no hope this side of death.

The [[White Tower|unstained tower]] breaks and [[Dumai's Wells|bends]] knee to the forgotten sign. The seas rage, and [[The Gathering Storm|stormclouds gather]] unseen. [[Seanchan (continent)|Beyond the horizon]], hidden fires swell, and serpents nestle in the bosom. What was exalted is cast down; what was cast down is raised up. Order burns to clear the path.
The fact that the price must be paid is proof that it is worth paying.
There is one rule, above all others, for being a man. Whatever comes, face it on your feet.
To stand against the Shadow so long as iron is hard and stone abides. To defend the Malkieri while one drop of blood remains. To avenge what cannot be defended.
You surrender after you're dead.
In war, you say a prayer for your dead and ride on, because there is always another fight over the next horizon.
There's an old saying here in the Borderlands: 'Better to have one woman on your side than ten men.'
The look of the [[Eyeless]] is fear.
If [[Rand|you]] are not mine, then you are dead.
I can show a tender, woman's heart when I choose.
Take what you can have. Rejoice in what you can save, and do not mourn your losses too long.
I would not mind you in my head if you were not so clearly mad.
The only way to live is to die. I must die. I deserve only death.
Pride fills me. I am sick with the pride that destroyed me.
A man without trust might as well be dead.
''The [[Wheel of Time]] and the wheel of a man's life turn alike without pity or mercy.''
You never escape the traps you spin yourself. Only a greater power can break a power, and then you're trapped again. Trapped forever so you cannot die.
What you want is what you cannot have. What you cannot have is what you want.
Death rides on my shoulder. Death walks in my footsteps. I am death.
''The wheel of a man's life. No mercy. No pity.''
Break the [[seals]]. Break the seals, and end it. Let me die forever.
Nothing ever goes as you expect. Expect nothing, and you will not be surprised. Expect nothing. Hope for nothing. Nothing.
Never prod at a woman unless you must. She will kill you faster than a man and for less reason, even if she weeps over it after.
<nowiki>[</nowiki>A woman<nowiki>]</nowiki> will kill you faster than a man and for less reason, even if she weeps over it after.
They will pay. I am the [[Lord of the Morning]].
I killed the whole world, and you can too, if you try hard.
A man who trusts everyone is a fool, and a man who trusts no one is a fool. We are all fools, if we live long enough.
I thought I could build, I was wrong. We are not builders, not you, or I, or the other one. We are destroyers. Destroyers.
Should and would build no bridges.
quotes.description_extra: , quoting [[Morgase Trakand]], who was possibly quoting [[Lini Eltring]]

quotes.quote: At my age, if I make it up, it's still an old saying.
An open sack hides nothing, and an open door hides little, but an open man is surely hiding something.
The pike does not ask the frog's permission before dining.
'Wish' and 'want' trip the feet, but 'is' makes the path smoother.
It's too late to change your mind after you've jumped off the cliff.
A slow horse does not always reach the end of the journey.
What can't be changed must be endured.
What you need isn't always what you want.
Stay and get married, or travel the [[Ways]]. Life is very unsettling with ''[[ta'veren]]'' for friends.
When fire threatens the trees, we do not run away and hope that the flames will not follow us. We fight. Now the [[Shadow]] is coming like wildfire, and we dare not run from it.
I am a free man, [[Aes Sedai]]. I am no Aes Sedai meat.
Time to toss the dice.
I am no bloody hero.
I'm a gambler, a farmboy, and I'm here to take command of your bloody army!
Trust is the color of a dark seed growing. Trust is the color of a heart's blood flowing. Trust is the color of a soul's last breath. Trust is the color of death.

A lion stuffed into a horse-stall might look like a peculiar joke, but a lion on the high plains was something very different. [[Toy]] was loose on the high plains, now. She felt a chill. What sort of man had she entangled herself with? After all this time, she realized, she had hardly a clue.
I'm no lord. I've more respect for myself than that.
''Dovie'andi se tovya sagain.''

quotes.description: The only rules [[Matrim Cauthon]] wishes to remember.
quotes.quote: Never kiss a girl whose brothers have knife scars. Never gamble without knowing a back way out.

We are going to tickle some [[Aes Sedai]] under the chin, rescue a mule, and put a snip-nosed girl on the [[Lion Throne]]. Oh, yes. That's [[Aviendha]]. Don't look at her cross-wise or she'll try to cut your throat and probably slit her own by mistake.
Dance well with a woman, and she's halfway yours.

I will wager two silver marks to two from [[Galad|each of you]] that I can beat [[Gawyn|both of you]] at once, just the way I said. You can't have fairer odds than that. There are two of you, and one of me, so two to one are fair odds.
An [[Aes Sedai]]'s gift is bait for a fish.
A pig painted gold is still a pig.
I'm no thief!
I may be a fool, but I intend to be a live fool.
One pretty woman means fun at the dance. Two pretty women mean trouble in the house. Three pretty women mean run for the hills.
''Caballein misain ye.''
''Deyeniye, dyu ninte concion ca'lyet ye.''
quotes.description_extra: - "Majesty, by your summons I do come."

quotes.quote: ''Inde muaghde [[Aes Sedai]] misain ye.''
''Mia ayende, [[Aes Sedai]].''
''Mia dovienya nesodhin soende.''
quotes.description_extra: - Unknown meaning, likely a fervent wish

quotes.quote: ''Mordero daghain pas duente cuebiyari.''
quotes.description_extra: - "No fear of Death holds my heart."

quotes.quote: ''Muad'drin tia dar allende caba'drin rhadiem.''
quotes.description_extra: - Roughly, "Foot soldiers pass forward, cavalry prepare!"

quotes.quote: ''Sa souvraya niende misain ye.''
quotes.description_extra: - "I am lost in my own mind."

quotes.quote: ''Sene sovya caba'donde ain dovienya.''
quotes.description_extra: - "Luck is a horse to ride like any other."

quotes.quote: Dance with her, and she will forgive much; dance well, and she will forgive anything.
''If the world is ending, a woman will want time to fix her hair. If the world's ending, a woman will take time to to tell a man something he's done wrong.''

Now. When the poor blind fool they've chosen out for their [[Amyrlin]] gets here, I will do the talking. She can't be very bright, or they'd never have been able to shove her into the job. Amyrlin Seat for a bloody village in the middle of bloody nowhere. You keep your mouths shut and curtsy for all you're worth, and I'll pull your bacon off the coals again.
The more tragic things get, the more I feel like laughing.
Blood and bloody ashes!
Everything always changes. The best plan lasts until the first arrow leaves the bow.
''Ninte calichniye no domashita.''

''How people see you first is what they hold hardest in their minds. It is the way of the world. You can step down from a throne, and even if you behave like a farmer in a pigsty, some part in each of them will remember that you did descend from a throne. But if they see only a young man first, a country man, they will resent him stepping up to his throne later, whatever his right, whatever his power.''
You cannot please everyone. You cannot soothe everyone.
I mean to deal with the world as I find the world, for as long as I can.
If you watch the wolf too hard a mouse will bite you in the ankle.
A bird cannot teach a fish to fly, nor a fish teach a bird to swim.
The best lie is often one too ridiculous to be taken for a lie.
I have made up my mind, young [[Tallanvor]], and I do not expect you to question me when I have done so.
I will NOT apologize.
Men always seemed to think violence could solve anything. If she had had a stout stick, she would have thumped all three of them about the shoulders until they saw reason.
I do not have to make sense.

Nynaeve shook her head. She supposed it was one way to find money for the poor. Simply rob anyone who was ''not'' poor. Of course, that would just make everyone poor in the end, but it might work for a time. She wondered if Uno and Ragan knew the whole of it. People who claimed they were collecting money to help others often had a way of letting a good bit stick in their own pockets, or else they liked the power that spreading it about gave them, liked it far too much. She had better feeling for the man who freely gave one copper from his own purse than for the fellow who wrested a gold crown from someone else's.
"Thank you, but we don't need any help," Nynaeve shouted. Politely.
"I won't shout at you," Nynaeve shouted.
My name is Nynaeve ti al'Meara Mandragoran. The message I want sent is this. My [[Lan|husband]] rides from [[World's End]] toward [[Tarwin's Gap]], toward [[Tarmon Gai'don]]. Will he ride alone?

Perhaps <nowiki>[</nowiki>''[[sul'dam]]''<nowiki>]</nowiki> do deserve to die and perhaps <nowiki>[</nowiki>[[Rand]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> would kill them. But men often mistake revenge and killing for justice. They seldom have the stomach for justice.
[[Egwene|You]] break your neck, and I'll see it mended just so I can break it again.
Caution once forgotten could be forgotten once too often.
I never heard of [[forkroot]], but walking seems to help the effects pass. You can walk most things off.
Close your mouth before you swallow a moth.
If you get yourself killed I will skin you alive.
Women do not become exhausted, they only exhaust others.
To anger the [[Ogier]] and pull the mountains down on your head.
They have caged [[Shadowkiller]]
''My duty is to do the things [[Rand]] cannot.''
Nobody tells us how to be men. We just are.
[[Rand]] is the one who's supposed to go mad, and here I am, talking to an axe!
If a sword had memory, it might be grateful to the forge fire, but never fond of it.

Do you believe that I could kill you? Right here, right now, without using a sword or the [[One Power|Power]]? Do you believe that if I simply willed it, the [[Pattern]] would bend around me and stop your heart? By... coincidence?
''Death is lighter than a feather, duty heavier than a mountain.''
I can rest when I'm dead.
I will see you tonight. Or I will see you dead.

He recalled countering [[Sammael]]'s last move with something particularly nasty, but he could not pull the memory to the surface. Not [[balefire]]. ''Mustn't use that. Threatens the fabric of the [[Pattern]]. Not even for Ilyena? I would burn the world and use my soul for tinder to hear her laugh again.''
Surprising what you can dig out of books if you read long enough, isn't it?

I am going to defeat them, [[Taim]]. All of them. They think they can tear everything down. It's always tearing down, never building up! I'm going to build something, leave something behind. Whatever happens, I will do that! I'll defeat the [[Dark One]]. And cleanse ''[[saidin]]'', so men don't have to fear going mad, and the world doesn't have to fear men channeling. I'll...
No man should have another man's voice in his head.
If I could find a way to escape my destiny, do I deserve to?
There was a price to be paid for any decision he made. There was a price for who he was. Other people paid it.
I am the [[Dragon Reborn]]. Denying won't change it. Wishing won't change it. I'm not the man you knew back in [[Emond's Field]]. Do you understand now? Do you?
quotes.description_extra: , and the other [[Two Rivers]] [[novices]] in the [[Culain's Hound]]

quotes.quote: "Take this message back to Sammael. Every death he has caused since waking, I lay at his feet and call due. Every murder he has ever done or caused, I lay at his feet and call due. He escaped justice in the [[Rorn M'doi]], and at [[Nol Caimaine]], and [[Sohadra]]...'" More of [[Lews Therin]]'s memories, but the pain of what had been done there, the agony of what Lews Therin's eyes had seen, burned across the [[Void]] as if Rand's. "...But I will see justice done now. Tell him, no truce with the [[Forsaken]]. No truce with the [[Shadow]]."

You are a very lucky man, [[Dimir Faral]]. You are going to watch you're friends hang. Then you'll be given a horse, and you will go tell [[Pedron Niall]] that one day I will hang him too for what happened here.

I will use anybody I must. You said it yourself; I am who I am. And I'm using myself up, [[Perrin]], because I have to. Just like I'll use anybody I have to. We don't have a choice anymore. Not me, not you, not anybody!

[[Sevanna]] wants my head, [[Taim]]. Apparently, she thought she could take it today. I mean to let her know her mistake. I told you to make weapons, Taim. Show me just how deadly they are. Disperse the [[Shaido]]. Break them.

I forget nothing, [[Aes Sedai]]. I said six could come, but I count nine. I said you would be on an equal footing with the [[White Tower|Tower]] emissaries, and for bringing nine, you will be. They are on their knees, Aes Sedai. Kneel!
Whatever can be done, can be undone.
The gloom dispersed, allowing him to see the sun hanging just above. Rand looked up at it. Then he smiled. Finally, he let out a deep-throated laugh, true and pure. It had been far too long.
The world had to be faced as it was, not as you wished it to be.
A man who will not die to save a woman is no man.
''Suravye ninto manshima taishite.''
''Tia mi aven Moridin isainde vadin.''
quotes.description: Inscription on the [[Horn of Valere]] - "The grave is no bar to my call."

quotes.quote: The louder a man tells you he's honest, the harder you must hold onto your purse.
If wishes were wings, pigs would fly.
If you pursue two hares, both will escape you.
An [[Aes Sedai]] is ten women in one skin.
The [[Wheel]] weaves as The Wheel wills.
''Tai'shar'' Manetheren! True blood of Manetheren!
I will find the song, or another will find the song, but the song will be sung this year or in a year to come. As it once was, so shall it be agian, world without end.
''Kiserai ti Wansho''.
''Tsingu ma choba.''
quotes.description_extra: for "I am unworthy of your honoring me."

quotes.quote: ''Tsingu ma choshih, T'ingshen.''
''Carai an Caldazar!''
quotes.description_extra: for "For the honor of the Red Eagle!"

quotes.quote: ''Al Caldazar!''
''Carai an [[Ellisande]]! Al Ellisande! Mordero daghain pas duente cuebiyar! Al Ellisande!''
quotes.description_extra: for "For the honor of the Rose of the Sun! For the Rose of the Sun! No death of fear holds my heart! For the Rose of the Sun!"

quotes.quote: ''Los Valdar Curbiyari! Los!''
Better to spit in a wolf's eye than to cross an [[Aes Sedai]].

And it was written that no hand but his should wield the [[Callandor|Sword]] held in the [[Stone of Tear|Stone]], but he did draw it out, like fire in his hand, and his glory did burn the world. Thus did it begin. Thus do we sing the Rebirth. Thus do we sing the beginning.
quotes.pseudosource: Do'in Toldara te, Songs of the Last Age

quotes.quote: And when the blood was sprinkled on ground where nothing could grow, the [[Children of the Dragon]] did spring up, the [[People of the Dragon]], armed to dance with death. And [[Car'a'carn|he]] did call them forth from [[Aiel Waste|the wasted lands]], and they did shake the world with battle.
A flapping tongue has killed more men than sudden storms ever did.
A flapping tongue can put you in the net instead of the fish.
When there are fish heads and blood in the water, you don't need to see the silverpike to know they are there.
Once you decide to gut a fish, there's no use waiting till it rots.
...but who can know the heart of a man? Not even he himself, I suspect. A man is the easiest animal to put on a leash, and the hardest to keep leashed. Even when he chooses it himself.
Most of those we call heroes only did what they had to do.
Trust is as slippery as a basket of eels sometimes.

I always thought the stole weighed about as much as three good men. The [[Amyrlin]] has few easy decisions to make, and fewer where she can be sure. Do what you must, and pay the price if you're wrong. Sometimes if you are right, too.
If you must drown or ride a lionfish, you ride and hope for the best.
In my day, girls jumped when a [[Wise One]] said jump, and continued jumping until they were told to stop. As I am still alive, it is still my day. Need I make myself clearer?
When a young woman's cheeks redden for no apparent reason, there is usually a man involved.
We are always more afraid than we wish to be, but we can always be braver than we expect.

Victors write history. Had I taken the [[Stone of Tear]], history would have shown I was born on the slopes of [[Dragonmount]], of a woman never touched by a man, and that the heavens opened up in radiance to herald my coming. The sort of thing they say about [[Rand|you]], now.
You cannot tell a man he has the power to make the earth shake, then expect him to walk small.
[[Asha'man]], kill!
In wars, boy, fools kill other fools for foolish causes.
Teach him how you will, a pig will never play the flute.
I'm only an old [[gleeman]], who could I possibly be dangerous to?
What did you do, boy? Stuff them up your sleeve?
Any fool knows men and women think differently at times, but the biggest difference is this. Men forget, but never forgive; women forgive, but never forget.
Better to try understanding the sun than a woman.
A man who, it was said, could play the [[Game of Houses]] in his sleep. It is a shame that such a man calls himself a simple [[gleeman]]. But such arrogance to keep the same name.
By the look of you, [[Nynaeve]], I could almost think you were angry, but I know you have such a sweet disposition people ask you to dabble your fingers in their tea.
Often you don't know whether a woman is friend, enemy or lover until it is too late. Sometimes, she is all three.
Horrible woman. If we had turned her loose on the [[Trollocs]], she'd have had them all sweeping and mopping.
[[Matrim Cauthon]] is my husband. Matrim Cauthon is my husband. Bloody Matrim Cauthon is my husband. That ''is'' the wording you used, is it not?
You may kiss me, [[Toy]].
Always plan for the worst, child; that way, all your surprises will be pleasant ones.
First things first; take care of what can be done now before worrying too long over what might never be.

quote.Rand: "How do you know when a woman wants to kill you?"

quotes.quote:
Ravens and crows. Rats. Mists and clouds. Insects and corruption. [[Bubble of evil|Strange events and odd occurrences]]. The ordinary twisted and strange. Wonders!
The dead are beginning to walk, and some see them. Others do not, but more and more, we all fear the night.
These have been our days. They rain upon us beneath a dead sky, crushing us with their fury, until as one we beg: "Let it begin!"
quotes.description_extra: , entry for The Feast of Freia

quotes.quote: At the end of time, when the many become one, [[The Gathering Storm|the last storm shall gather]] its angry winds to destroy a land already dying. And at its center, [[Rand|the blind man]] shall stand upon his [[Dragonmount|own grave]]. [[Veins of Gold|There he shall see again]], and weep for what has been wrought.
They could not break or bend him. It was done.

quote.Verin: By the way, that dress you are wearing is green.

quote.Egwene: Egwene frowned at the nonsense, glancing down at her dress. Of course it wasn't green. What was Verin saying? Had the woman become—

quotes.quote: [[Aes Sedai]] are tricksome. They don't lie, not right out, but the truth an Aes Sedai tells you is not always the truth you think it is.
The truth an [[Aes Sedai]] tells you is not always the truth you think it is.
An Aes Sedai never lies, but the truth she speaks may not be the truth you think you hear.
Life is a dream from which we all must wake before we can dream again.
Life is a dream.
Better ten days of love than years of regretting.
[[Rand al'Thor]], is a mule-headed, stone-willed fool of a... a... a man!
Do not trouble trouble till trouble troubles you.
Death comes for us all. We can only choose how to face it when it comes.
A woman's flaming rights are whatever she flaming says they are. That's what women in [[Shienar]] say, anyway.
Oh, Light, why do I have [[Rand|a madman]] in my head? Why? Why?
If you're going to fight a battle, who better to pay the butcher's bill than men who want you dead?
A woman's eyes cut deeper than a knife
I always get what I want in the end. And I think I want... ornamental ironwork. For the windows of my bedchamber.
I'll not have you bleeding to death on me. That would be just like you, to die and leave me the work of burying you. You have no consideration.
Come against me, if you dare! I ''am'' the storm! Come if you dare, [[Shai'tan]]! I am the [[Dragon Reborn]]!

And the [[Shadow]] fell upon the Land, and the World was riven stone from stone. The oceans fled, and the mountains were swallowed up, and the nations were scattered to the eight corners of the World. The moon was as blood, and the sun was as ashes. The seas boiled, and the living envied the dead. All was shattered, and all but memory lost, and one memory above all others, of him who brought the Shadow and the [[Breaking of the World]]. And him they named [[Dragon]].
Whoever reads this, if any remain to read it, weep for us who have no more tears. Pray for us who are damned alive.
quotes.description_extra: , quoting a manuscript believed to have been written during the [[Breaking]]

quotes.quote: I crafted these. I made them to never break. But I knew, as I did it, that they would eventually fail. Everything eventually fails when [[Dark One|he]] touches it
<nowiki>[</nowiki>[[Mat]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> headed back for [[The White Crescent]], uncaring of mud or the damp heat. He could feel the dice tumbling inside his head.

If [[Couladin]] really was leading, if he thought [[Rand]] was with the pikes, if the pikes could hold until the horse arrived ... A lot of ifs. Mat could hear those dice rolling in his head again. This was the biggest gamble he had ever taken in his life. He wondered how long it was until nightfall; a man should be able to make his way out in the night. He wished those dice would get out of his head, or else fall so he knew what they showed. Scowling into the rain, he booted Pips on down the hillside.

[[Mat|He]] was drawn to battle or it to him. Nobody could have tried harder to avoid one on the other side of the [[Alguenya]]. Even [[Talmanes]] had commented on it. Until the second time his careful creeping away from one lot of [[Andorans]] took them where there was no choice but to fight another. And every time he could feel the dice rolling in his head; it was almost like a warning that a fight was just over the next hill, now.

The largest palace he had seen yet filled one entire side of the square, all domes and spires and colonnades three and four stories above the ground. <nowiki>[...]</nowiki> It was a picture of tranquility. [[Mat]] did not understand why he suddenly felt the dice rolling in his head.
He knew that sensation well. Sometimes he felt it when his luck was running strong in the gambling. It was always there when a battle was in the offing. And it seemed to come when there was a vital decision to make, the sort where the wrong choice might well get his throat cut.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
"Mistress [[Anan]], I feel like I've come home."
The odd thing was, the dice had stopped rolling in his head.

A white-haired man with a hooked nose. That old man had been at the [[Silver Circuit]], standing not far from the woman who had just gone into [[Carridin]]'s rented palace. Turning his hat in his hands, he frowned uneasily at the palace. The Mire never held a bog like this one. He could feel the dice tumbling in his head suddenly, and that was always a bad sign.

Normally, displays of wealth made Mat feel comfortable. For one thing, where there was money, some might stick to his fingers. This time he felt impatient, more so by the step. And anxious. The last time he had felt the dice rolling so hard in his head was just before he found himself with three hundred of the Band, a thousand of [[Gaebril]]'s [[White Lions]] on a ridge to his front and another thousand coming hard up the road behind him, when all he had been trying to do was ride away from the entire mess. That time he had avoided the chop by the grace of other men's memories and more luck than he had a right to. The dice almost always meant danger, and something else he had not figured out yet. The prospect of having his skull cracked was not enough, and once or twice there had been no possibility of such, yet the upcoming likelihood of [[Mat Cauthon]] dead in some spectacular fashion seemed the most usual cause. Unlikely, maybe, in the [[Tarasin Palace]], but unlikely did not make the dice go away.

<nowiki>[</nowiki>[[Mat]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> would as soon tangle himself with that fox-faced [[Darkfriend]] as with a queen. Not looking at all was difficult, but he managed. Most likely she would call guards rather than draw the gem-encrusted dagger thrust behind a woven-gold belt to match the collar her marriage knife hung from. Maybe that was why the dice were still rolling in his head. The possibility of an encounter with the headsman would set them spinning if anything did.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
No telling when those bloody dice would stop or for what.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Tylin's stare made him nervous. And those dice still rattled about in his skull. He wanted out of there.

Mat wanted to back away; even [[Teslyn]] stood close enough to be almost touching him. <nowiki>[...]</nowiki> Those dice in his head could have nothing to do with this pair, or they would have stopped spinning.

This could have qualified to start those dice rolling in his head—a head that would have been cracked open for sure without the luck of that fellow stepping on the one board in the whole inn that would squeak—but the bloody things were still tumbling. He did not like it.<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Somehow he would see those two women safely out of [[Ebou Dar]]. The trouble was, he did not have a clue how. He wished those bloody dice would stop, and be done with it.

The entire encounter with the three beggars had lasted only a minute or two and had been seen by no one. In this city, you could find three or four fights in a day if you were not careful, but the odds of facing two sets of robbers in one day seemed about as great as the odds of the Civil Guard refusing a bribe. What was happening to his luck? If only those bloody dice would stop rolling in his head.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
A gilded woman? In his room? The chest of gold rested now in a small hollow beneath the kitchen floor, in front of one of the stoves, but the dice in his head drummed like thunder suddenly.<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
On the one hand, a chance to talk with Birgitte—Birgitte! he doubted he would ever get over the shock—but on the other, he doubted he would be able to hear the music downstairs for the noise of those dice rattling in his skull. She must be a key to it, somehow. A man with any brains would climb out the window right now.

Mat knew he was in trouble from the day he moved into the Tarasin Palace. He could have refused. Just because the flaming dice started or stopped did not mean he had to ''do'' anything; usually when they stopped spinning, it was too late not to do something.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Why ''had'' the dice in his head stopped tumbling as soon as Elayne mentioned these bloody rooms?
When he woke for his third morning in the Tarasin Palace, the dice were rolling in his head.
Those bloody dice were bouncing around in his skull. Besides, he had important business to see to. The dice had never had anything to do with finding something, but....

"Sometimes it's fun to be looked at," she said, poking him in the ribs, when he commented. Her grin would have done for Nalesean saying how much fun it was to pinch serving girls. "There's a lot more to it than feather dancers wore, but not enough to it to slow me down, and anyway, I cannot see we'll have to move quickly on this side of the river." The dice rattled in his head.
Light, what was he going to do? Move back to the inn? Burn why the dice had stopped before.

His hands ran along his spear—an ''ashandarei'', Birgitte called it—unthinkingly fingering the haft as if he might need to defend himself. The dice tumbled inside his head fiercely, yet that had nothing to do with his uneasiness. The source of that was Tylin.

Her tone was so mild that Elayne must have passed on the truth about Tylin, but if anything, that only soured his mood further. He did not want ''anyone'' to know. Bloody useless! But those dice were still rattling around in his head. "Maybe Moghedien likes back doors," he said dryly.
Three hours back in the Tarasin Palace, the dice still bouncing in his head, and he wanted to kick something. Or somebody.
"What happened to my bloody luck?" he shouted. He had time for that. And just time to realize, as brick and timbers crashed down on him, that the dice in his head had just stopped dead.

Mat groaned. It was not his leg, this time, or the fact that every man in [[Ebou Dar]] seemed to be choosing the bosom they rested their heads on except for Mat Cauthon. Those bloody dice had just started tumbling in his head again. Something bad was coming his way. Something very bad.

Mat always noticed horses, even if with only half his mind or less. A fat Cairhienin in a coat as drab as those of his wagon drivers was shouting angrily about the delay and letting his fine bay mare dance nervously. A very good conformation on that mare. She would go to an officer, most likely. What was going to happen when the dice stopped?

As soon as he returned to the Palace, Tylin would start cosseting and petting him. It would not have been that bad, really—not really—except that she did not care who saw her caress his cheeks and whisper endearments in his ear, even her son. Besides, what if the dice in his head stopped when he reached her? Possessive was hardly the word for Tylin these days. Blood and ashes, the woman might have decided to marry him! He did not want to marry, not yet, but he knew who he was going to marry, and it was not Tylin Quintara Mitsobar. Only, what could he do if she decided differently?

He had to have a room, a garret in some inn's attic the size of a wardrobe, anything, where he could hide away gold a little at a time, or he had to have a chance with the dice, one or the other. Luck or no luck, though, he eventually realized that he was going to find neither today. And those bloody dice were still tumbling in his head, tumbling.

He ached from head to foot, the dice rattled warning inside his skull, and he hardly noticed either thing. He was too busy trying to watch every direction at once, and wondering just how small a hole that thing could get through. He found himself uneasily eyeing cracks between the square's paving stones. Though it hardly seemed likely the <nowiki>[</nowiki>''[[gholam]]''<nowiki>]</nowiki> would come at him in the open.

Tylin could tickle him under the chin the rest of his life if it kept him off the stake. Light, he wished those bloody dice in his head would just stop and get it over with! No, that was a lie. Since he had finally realized what they meant, he had never wanted the dice to stop.

It was not the presence of Suroth or the strangers that jerked him to a halt, though. The dice had stopped, landing with a thunder that made his skull ring. That had never happened before. He stood there waiting for one of the Forsaken to leap out of the flames in the marble fireplace, or the earth to swallow the Palace beneath him.
"You aren't listening to me, pigeon," Tylin cooed in dangerous tones. "I said, take yourself down to the kitchens and have a pastry until I have time for you. Have a bath while you're about it." Her dark eyes glittered. "We will discuss your mud later."
In a daze, he ran it through again in his head. He had walked into the room, the dice had stopped, and ... Nothing had happened. Nothing!
"This man has been set upon," the tiny, veiled figure said, rising. Her tone turned cold as the wind outside. "You told me the streets were safe, Suroth! I am displeased."
Something ''had'' to happen! It already should have! Something always happened when the dice stopped.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Any other time, those pink ribbons would have had him gibbering. He never should have tried to get his own back with her. Even the ''gholam'' did not occupy much of his thoughts. The dice had stopped and ... What? He had come face-to-face, or near enough, with three people he had not met before, but that could not be it. Maybe it was something to do with Tylin becoming one of the Blood. But always before, when the dice stopped, something had happened to him, personally.

For a moment, Mat had cursed the Windfinders for moving sooner than he had been promised. But the dice in his head had stopped, he realized. Why? It made him want to curse all over again, but there was no time for even that.

The plump-faced woman made a clicking sound, as you might to a pet dog, and twitched the ''a'dam,'' and the ''damane'' followed her on. They were looking for ''marath'damane'' trying to escape the leash, not ''damane.'' Mat still thought he might choke. The sound of dice rolling had started up again in his head, loud enough to rival the occasional rumble of distant thunder. Something was going to go wrong; he knew it.
Some folks would not resist the temptation of a little more gold, either. In any case, no warning dice tumbled in his head. And there were people inside those canvas walls he could not leave behind.
It was going to take some time yet before the show was ready to travel, but that was not what made Mat groan. He had just heard those bloody dice start rattling in his head again.

Mat did not know whether to curse or weep. With the soldiers gone and Ebou Dar about to be left in his dust, there seemed no reason for the dice, but there never was a bloody reason he could see until it was too late. Whatever was coming might lie days in the future or only an hour, but he had never been able to figure it out ahead of time. The only certainties were that something important—or dire—was going to happen and that he would not be able to avoid it. Sometimes, like that night at the gate, he did not understand why the dice had been tumbling even after they stopped. All he really knew for sure was that however much the dice made him twitch like a goat with the itch, once they started, he did not want them to stop ever. But they did. Sooner or later, they always did.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
"There's nothing to settle," he told her. "I was never your hired hand, and that's that." Somehow, her face managed to grow harder, as good as shouting that she did not see matters like that. The woman was as tenacious as a snapping turtle, but there had to be some way to pry her jaws from his leg. Burn him if he wanted to be alone with the dice rolling in his head, yet that was better than having to listen to them while arguing with her. "I'm going to see Tuon before we leave." The words popped out of his mouth before they were clear in his head. He realized that they had been lying there for some time, though, murky and slowly solidifying.

He had thought Egeanin was going to swallow her tongue while he was explaining to Luca. Maybe she had known how Tuon would take <nowiki>[</nowiki>being a traitorous servant in Mat's cover story<nowiki>]</nowiki>. Light, he almost wished the dice would stop. How could a man think with that in his head?

He was not afraid of seeing Tuon again. Of course not. He had stayed away, after sticking her into that wagon, to give her time to settle down and collect herself. That was all. Only ... Calm, Domon had called her, and it was true. Kidnapped in the middle of the night, snatched out into a storm by people who would as soon have cut her throat as look at her, as far as she knew, and she had been by far the coolest of them all. Light, she could have planned it herself, that was how upset she was! It had made him feel as if the point of a knife were tickling between his shoulder blades then, and the knife was back again just thinking about her. And those dice were rattling away inside his skull.

He did whimper this time, and not because <nowiki>[</nowiki>[[Tuon]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> had read the Old Tongue inscription on his ''ashandarei.'' A bloody stone would have whimpered. The dice had stopped as soon as he touched her hand. Light, what had happened?
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
''Something'' had happened, or the dice would not have stopped. A thought came that made his hair want to stand on end. This was the second time they had stopped in Tuon's presence. The third, counting the gate leading out of Ebou Dar. Three bloody times, and all tied to her.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
It still seemed impossible. And it did not seem at all important compared to the dice stopping. What had ''happened''? He had shaken hands with Tuon, that was all. Shaken hands and made a bargain. He meant to keep his side, but what had the dice told him? That she would keep hers? Or that she would not? For all he knew, Seanchan noblewomen were in the habit of marrying—what was it she had said she was going to make him?—a cupbearer—maybe they married cupbearers all the time.
He could not help wondering, what had Rand been doing when the dice stopped?

On the third day after leaving the river, they reached the salt town of Jurador, and he told Tuon that he would <nowiki>[</nowiki>take her shopping<nowiki>]</nowiki>. She smiled at him, and the dice in his head stopped dead. He would always remember that. She smiled, and ''then'' the dice stopped. A man could weep!

Riding along and waiting for Tuon to shout. She had given her word, but a prisoner would say anything to get the shackles loosened. All she had to do was raise her voice, and summon a thousand Seanchan soldiers for rescue. The dice bounced and spun in Mat's head. Riding along, waiting for the Dark One's eyes.

Sometimes, you just had to trust to luck. The trouble was, when he woke this morning, the dice had again been tumbling in his head. They were bouncing off the inside of his skull still.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Tuon did not say a word. She just stood there looking up at Mat, waiting, big eyes getting cooler by the second. The dice bounced and rattled in his head. Well, he only hesitated a heartbeat before jerking his head to send the Redarm away. Maybe two heartbeats. He had to trust his luck. Trust her word. ''Trust is the sound of death.'' He stepped on that thought hard. This was no song, and no old memory could guide him. The dice inside his skull kept spinning.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
The stare Latelle shifted to Mat was not worried, just stone hard. “Remember,” she said quietly, “if you send us to the gallows, you send yourself.” Then she sniffed and went back to studying the people waiting to get in. Latelle was even better than Luca at judging the weight of a purse before the drawstrings were undone. She was also ten times tougher than her husband. The dice tumbled on. Whatever had set them spinning, he had not yet reached the fateful point. The deciding point.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Had any of those people cast shadows before they vanished? He could not recall any of them breathing a mist, either. It hardly seemed to matter. They were gone, and he was not going to think about where they had come from or where they had gone. Probably something to do with being ''ta'veren.'' He was going to put it out of his head. He was. The dice rattling away left room for nothing else.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Luckily, he had tucked a fat purse of gold into his coat pocket. None of it seemed to be right, though. Inevitably, Tuon shook her head, and the pair of them glided away into the crowd with Mat hurrying to keep up as far as the next shop showing silks. The dice continued to bounce off the inside of his skull.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Who could think about coats when he was waiting for those bloody dice to stop? Just a little embroidery, on the sleeves and shoulders.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Closing his eyes, he spun in a circle in the middle of the street and took a step. At random. He bumped into someone solid, hard enough to make them both grunt. <nowiki>[...]</nowiki> Mat did not care. He was facing straight at one of the two shops. Pulling his hat down tight, he ran. The dice ''were'' rolling faster.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Juilin came running up, for a wonder without Thera or his red cap. The thief-catcher's face could have been carved from ancient oak. Eyeing the people flowing past them into the show, he pitched his voice low. Low and urgent. “I was coming to find you. It's Egeanin; she's been... hurt. Come quickly.”
The man's tone said enough, but worse, Mat realized the dice in his head were drumming, now.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
"Think what you'll have if a thousand Seanchan find you here tomorrow." Mat's voice was as cold as he could make it. If he failed, the Seanchan would run Luca's show down in short order however fast they flogged their horses. Luca knew it, too, from the twist of his mouth, as if he had just bitten a rotting plum. Mat made himself ignore the man. The dice were drumming hard, but they had not stopped yet.<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
If he turned back, he could be a good distance the other side of Jurador by sunset, in company with Thom and Juilin and the others. With Tuon. With the Seanchan knowing to hunt Mat Cauthon. The man who had kidnapped the Daughter of the Nine Moons could not own enough luck to get off with being made ''da'covale.'' And sometime tomorrow or the next day, they would plant Luca on an impaling stake. Luca and Latelle, Petra and Clarine and the rest. A thicket of impaling stakes. The dice rattled and bounced in his head.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Mat felt something flicker and die inside him. He did not know what. Something. The dice rolled like thunder. "Shoot," he said.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Slowly, she toppled from the horse, sliding down the slope, rolling, bouncing off saplings, tumbling faster and faster until she splashed into the stream. For a moment, she floated facedown against the bank, and then the current caught her and pulled her away, skirts billowing up on the water. Slowly she drifted toward the Eldar. Maybe, eventually, she would reach the sea. And that made three. It hardly seemed to matter that the dice had stopped. That made three. ''Never again,'' he thought as Renna floated out of sight around a bend. ''If I die for it, never again.''

He had spent a night of bleak dreams about corpses floating downstream and woken to the dice spinning in his head, always a bad sign, and now they seemed to be bouncing off the inside of his skull harder than before.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
He was always tempted to just sit quietly somewhere when the dice were clicking in his head, some place nothing seemed likely to happen, waiting for the dice to stop, and though he would have enjoyed watching some of the female acrobats, a number of whom wore as little as the contortionists, he set out to walk the half mile to Jurador, eyeing everyone on the wide, hard-packed clay road closely. There was a purchase he hoped to make.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
The dice had never before signaled a fight—battles, yes, but never a dust-up in the street—yet he walked very carefully indeed. Not that that would help, of course. When the dice stopped, they stopped, and that was that.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
He put on his flat-brimmed hat and left, the dice rattling away.<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
When he got back to the show at midday, riding the razor bareback because of his aching hip and with the dice rattling in his head, <nowiki>[...]</nowiki> The dice said something was going to happen, something fateful to Mat bloody Cauthon, but what? There had been times when the dice stopped and he still had no idea what happened.
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
In truth, he hesitated about going to Tuon at all with the dice drumming in his head. They had stopped too often in her presence, and he still did not know the why for a single one of those times. Not for certain. Maybe the first time, it had just been meeting her.With Seanchan camped across the road and Aes Sedai arguing and women channeling as if they had never heard of the Seanchan and the dice spinning in his head, not even winning two games of stones from Tuon that night could make him feel anything but wary. He went to sleep—on the floor, since it was Domon's turn to use the second bed; Egeanin always got the other—with the dice bouncing off the insides of his skull, but he was sure that tomorrow had to be better than today.

In his experience, Aes Sedai carried trouble in their belt pouches and seldom were shy about scattering it, never mind who might be in the way. No, with the dice bouncing inside his head, he could have done without Aes Sedai within ten miles.
The dice rattled away so that Mat was always wondering what lay beyond the next bend in the road or what was catching him up from behind. It was enough to give a man hives.

For a moment, as he shook her hand, he was sure the dice had stopped, but a heartbeat later they were rattling again. It must have been imagination. After all, this agreement with Aludra might help the Band, and incidentally Mat Cauthon, stay alive, yet it could hardly be called fateful. He would still have to fight those battles, and however you planned, however well-trained your men were, luck played its part, too, bad as well as good, even for him. These dragons would not change that. But were the dice bouncing as loudly? He thought not, yet how could he be sure? Never before had they slowed without stopping. It had to be his imagination.

It started raining before the hole was knee-deep, a cold driving rain, and by the time he was done, he was soaked to the skin and mud to his waist. A fine end to a fine night, with the dice bouncing around his skull.

"It's good you've acknowledged that you don't expect to be her equal, too."
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Mat ground his teeth to keep from shouting a curse. He had acknowledged ''what''? No wonder a set of bloody dice had stopped. Tuon would let him forget this when it snowed on Sunday. He was certain sure of that.

"There's no dancing away from this one," Mat said frowning up at the wagon door. The dice clicked away in his head. "Not for me." He was not sure he really wanted to dance away anymore, but want and wish as he might, he was well and truly caught.<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
Mistress Anan glanced at the wagon, frowning. “That girl is playing a game with you as surely as you are playing one with her. Not the same game that you are. She's more like a general plotting a battle than a woman being courted. If she learns you're moonstruck with her, though, she'll still gain the advantage. I am willing to let you have an even chance. Or as near to one as any man has with a woman of any brains. Do we have an agreement?"
"We do," he replied fervently. "That we do." He would not have been surprised if the dice stopped then, but they went on bouncing.
All seemed right in the world. Even the dice bouncing in his head could steal nothing from that.

The dice in his head bounced and rattled even when the thunder was loudest. "Another game, Thom?"
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
"Burn me for a fool," he muttered. "I'll go <nowiki>[</nowiki>to rescue [[Moiraine]]<nowiki>]</nowiki>."
Thunder crashed deafeningly right atop a flash of lightning so bright it shone through the tent canvas. When the rumbling booms faded, there was dead silence in his head. The last set of dice had stopped. He could have wept.

They had ridden off up the road from Maderin as if setting out for Lugard, then taken to the forest as soon as the last farms were out of sight. The moment they entered the trees, the dice started up in his head again. That was the other thing that soured his mood, those bloody dice drumming inside his head for two days. There hardly seemed any way they could stop here in the forest. What kind of momentous event could happen in the woods? Still, he had stayed well clear of the small villages they had passed. Sooner or later the dice would stop, though, and he could only wait for it.

Then Mat recognized the other rider, whose cloak was flailing behind him, and felt as if he had been punched in the belly. He would not have been surprised in the least had the dice stopped then, but they kept bouncing off the inside of his skull. What in the Light was [[Talmanes]] bloody well doing in Altara?

"[[Matrim Cauthon]] is my husband. Matrim Cauthon is my husband. Bloody Matrim Cauthon is my husband. That ''is'' the wording you used, is it not?"
<nowiki>[...]</nowiki>
It took a minute before Mat could speak. Burn him, it seemed to take a bloody hour before he could move. When he could, he snatched off his hat, strode to Tuon and seized the razor's bridle. She looked down at him, cool as any queen on a bloody throne. All those battles with the flaming dice rattling away in his head, all those skirmishes and raids, and they had to stop when she said a few words. Well, at least this time he knew what had happened that was bloody fateful for Mat bloody Cauthon.

At <nowiki>[</nowiki>the moment Mat nodded agreement to [[Hinderstap]]'s rules<nowiki>]</nowiki>, the dice started rattling in his head. ''Burn it!'' He decided to ignore them. They were never any help anyway.

And the dice stopped rattling in his head. It was so sudden, the silence so unexpected, that he froze. It was enough to make him think he'd made the wrong decision <nowiki>[</nowiki>to finish the [[Hinderstap]] bet<nowiki>]</nowiki>.

The dice he had tossed—all three of them—had landed still and were balanced on their ''corners''. Light! He had tossed coins so they fell on their sides before, but he had never done anything like this.
Right there, all of a sudden, the dice started rattling inside his head. He almost jumped clear to the ceiling. ''Blood and bloody ashes!'' Those dice in his head never meant anything good. They only stopped when something changed, something that usually meant bad news for poor Matrim Cauthon.
"I counted my horses again," Mat said. Those dice were still rattling in his head, burn them. "I did another count of the Band's horses. Turns out, we have some to spare. You may take them."

"That went well," Mat decided, hands on hips. "I worried <nowiki>[</nowiki>[[Elayne]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> wouldn't bite, but I think I reeled her in pretty well." Though the bloody dice were still rolling in his head.
Mat pulled off his black scarf, leaving it on the floor. It had a hole in it now anyway. He stepped out into the night, and the moment he did, the dice stopped thundering in his head.

"Let it be done," Elayne said. "I hope you know what you're doing, Mat."
As she spoke, the dice started tumbling inside his head.
Those dice rattled in his head, just as they'd been doing ever since Egwene gave him control of all of the armies of the Light. Being bloody ''ta'veren'' was not worth two beans.

Mat turned northward again. A cool, somehow ''familiar'' wind blew across him, rippling his long coat, brushing at his hat. He narrowed his eye. Rand was tugging on him.
The dice still tumbled in his head.
"Go fetch <nowiki>[</nowiki>Lady Tinna<nowiki>]</nowiki>," Mat said. Those dice kept rattling in his head.

They could not fight either one.

Wanting won't make a stone cheese, but he still smells like cheese to me.
Light! Two ''[wives]''! Oh, burn me! He's the luckiest man in the world or the biggest fool since creation!
You were never meant for greatness, [[Asmodean]], only to follow those who are great.
I will run no more.
Fall in love with a man, and you ended up doing laundry, even if it did belong to another man.
Sleep well and wake, [[Rand al'Thor]].
Sleep well and wake.
It seems to me that kings — and queens — can be fools when they forget what they are and act like who they are, but they're worse when they only remember what they are and forget who.
If you fell head first into a pigsty, you'd try to convince everybody you did it on purpose.
Schemes within schemes. The Great Serpent is a good sign for you Aes Sedai, I think. Someday you may swallow yourselves by accident.
I know how to take a man out of his miseries. Give him a swift kick, or else get him drunk and find him a pr—

Once he had a grove of oaks chopped down because they were looking at him. And then insisted they be given decent funerals; he gave the oration. Do you have any idea how long it takes to dig graves for twenty-three oak trees?

When I first slept in a saddle, [[Muad Cheade]] was [[Marshal-General]]. The man was as mad as a hare in spring thaw. Twice every day he searched his bodyservant for poison, and he drank nothing but vinegar and water, which he claimed was sovereign against the poison the fellow fed him, but he ate everything the man prepared for as long as I knew him.
He might have been insane, but he could outgeneral anyone I ever saw. He never lost a battle. He never even came close to losing.
Absently he fingered the neat slice across the shoulder of his coat. Good shooting, at a moving target only half-seen through trees. He could have admired it more had he not been the target.
He strains to hear a whisper who refuses to hear a shout.
And as for words of wisdom, the first she had heard out of him had been a fervent promise never to throw a rock at anyone again, offered after she had paddled his young backside for it.

I once saw a man hanging from a cliff. The brink was crumbling under his fingers, and the only thing near enough to grasp was a tuft of grass, a few long blades with roots barely clinging to the rock. The only chance he had of climbing back up on the cliff. So he grabbed it. He had to know it would pull free.

Mat was caught up in it, now. He more than merely liked gambling, and battle was a gamble to make dicing in taverns a thing for children and toothless invalids. Lives were the stake here, your own and other men's, men who were not even there. Make the wrong wager, a foolish bet, and cities died, or whole nations. [[Natael]]'s somber music was fit accompaniment. At the same time, this was a game that set the blood racing.
Oh, I do remember you. The one with the fla—the mouth. [[Ragan]] thought you could skin and butcher a blo—a bull at ten paces with your tongue. [[Chaena]] and [[Nangu]] thought fifty.
That was all he ever really wanted from women; a smile, a dance, a kiss, and to be remembered fondly.
The Creator made women to please the eye and trouble the mind.
Take what you want, and pay for it.

We are alike in many ways, you and I. There is a darkness in us. Darkness, pain, death. They radiate from us. If ever you love a woman, [[Rand]], leave her and let her find another. It will be the best gift you can give her.
''We all make our limits. And we set them further out than we have any right.''
The more women there are about, the softer a wise man steps.
A man is a man, on a throne or in a pigsty.
''A shoat squealing under a fence just attracts the fox, when it should be trying to run.''

quotes.quote: When the honey's out of the comb, there's no putting it back.
When a woman says she will obey you, of her own will, it is time to sleep lightly and watch your back.
All he wanted from life was some good wine, a game of dice, and a pretty girl or three.
You will do well.

quotes.quote: If you ever meet a [[Malkieri]], you tell him [[Jain Farstrider]] died clean.
''Peel the apple in your hand, girl, not the one on the tree.''
''Tears are for after; they just waste time before.''
''When a woman plays the fool, look for the man''

''Flesh so fine, so fine to tear, to gnash the skin; skin to strip, to plait, so nice to plait the strips, so nice, so red the drops that fall; blood so red, so red, so sweet; sweet screams, pretty screams, singing screams, scream your song, sing your screams...''

''...blood so sweet, so sweet to drink the blood, the blood that drips, drips, drops so red; pretty eyes, fine eyes, I have no eyes, pluck the eyes from out of your head; grind your bones, split your bones inside your flesh, suck your marrow while you scream; scream, scream, singing screams, sing your screams...''
The [[old blood]] sings.

The old blood is strong in [[Emond’s Field]], and the [[old blood]] sings. I knew you for what you were the moment I saw you. No Aes Sedai can stand in the presence of a woman who can channel, or who is close to her change, and not feel it.
The blood of [[Aemon]]’s line is still strong in the [[Two Rivers]]. The [[old blood]] still sings.

I’ve heard that it can happen, sometimes. Heard, though I never really thought. . . . It was your roots, boy. A line running from you to your father to your grandfather, right on back to [[Manetheren]], and maybe beyond. Well, now you know your family is old. You ought to let it go at that and be glad. Most people don’t know much more than that they had a father.
He will be of the ancient blood, and raised by the [[old blood]].
The [[Old Blood]] comes again.
Blood of [[Aiel|our blood]] mixed with the [[old blood]], raised by an [[Manetheren|ancient blood]] not ours.

Most of his memories were from [[Manetheren]]. Some of those he had had before the twisted doorway. Moiraine said it was the [[Old Blood]] coming out. Just as long as it did not come out of his veins.

I can find work for gleemen, too. Idle hands are idle hands.

Balwer believed nothing, perhaps not even in Darkfriends, or the Dark One. If Balwer did believe in anything, it was looking over men's shoulders, listening to their whispers, rooting out their secrets.

It's a wonderful ego stroking. And it's also astonishing. I've known it about it for some time, and I'm not certain I'm over it yet, really. It does sort of make me want to drop my jaw. I find it astonishing. And, as I say, it's very very flattering, very flattering.

How do you fight someone smarter than yourself? The answer is simple. You make [[Graendal|her]] think that you are sitting down across the table from her, ready to play her game. Then you punch her in the face as hard as you can.
The woman would not believe the sky was blue without proof.
It was said she would not believe it was morning till she saw the sun for herself.

[[Tear]] is the greatest port on the [[Sea of Storms]], and the [[Stone of Tear]] is the fortress that guards it. The Stone is said to be the first fortress built after the [[Breaking of the World]], and in all this time it has never fallen, though more than one army has tried. One of the [[Prophecies]] says that the Stone of Tear will never fall until the [[People of the Dragon]] come to the Stone. Another says the Stone will never fall till the [[Sword That Cannot Be Touched]] is wielded by the [[Dragon]]’s hand. The fall of the Stone will be one of the major proofs that the Dragon has been reborn. May the Stone stand till I am dust.

The [[Dark One]] is after you three, one or all, and if I let you go running off wherever you want to go, he will take you. Whatever the Dark One wants, I oppose, so hear this and know it true. Before I let the Dark One have you, I will destroy you myself.
